p33CVV29OG8.summary: Python core developer Raymond Hettinger explains how Python's dictionary implementation evolved into the compact, ordered dict in Python 3.6. He uses pictures and small bits of pure Python, and covers key-sharing, compaction and versioning.
p33CVV29OG8.why: HN treats it as the definitive, engaging talk on hash table internals and Python dict ordering, and recommends it in tech-talk lists.

pgoetgxecw8.summary: Casey Muratori's first refterm lecture lays out philosophies of optimization, distinguishing optimization from non-pessimization, which means avoiding needless work. It uses his fast terminal renderer project to show how fast computers really are.
pgoetgxecw8.why: HN returns to it constantly in software performance debates as the primer on non-pessimization and why modern software is slow.

p2LZLYcu_JY.summary: A full upload of Alan Kay's 1987 talk, with demos of several Smalltalk-era software systems and ideas about visual, kinesthetic and symbolic reasoning. It includes a Smalltalk program written by a 12-year-old and footage of the Rand tablet.
p2LZLYcu_JY.why: HN recommends it as a favourite tech talk full of good ideas from forgotten 1980s software, worth watching in full.

pwaWilO_Pig.summary: Joe Rogan interviews Matthew Walker, Berkeley neuroscience professor and author of Why We Sleep. They discuss what sleep does for the brain and body, the effects of sleep deprivation, and sleep myths.
pwaWilO_Pig.why: HN readers recommend it as an accessible, motivating summary of Why We Sleep for people who will not read the book.

pW-SOdj4Kkk.summary: Jonathan Blow's DevGAMM 2019 talk argues that software knowledge is being lost between generations and that growing layers of abstraction could lead to a decline in technological civilization.
pW-SOdj4Kkk.why: A perennial HN reference for arguments that software is getting worse and that hard-won knowledge is disappearing.

pTn6Ewhb27k.summary: Veritasium explains why the one-way speed of light has never been measured, only the round-trip speed, since measuring it requires synchronized clocks that assume the answer. It explores the implications for relativity.
pTn6Ewhb27k.why: Used as the standard reference in threads about light speed, clock synchronization and untestable assumptions in physics.

prXuyMCgbTc.summary: In this 2019 GDC session, Petri Purho of Nolla Games explains the technical side of Noita's physics engine, including scaling a falling-sand simulation to large continuous worlds and adding destructible rigid bodies. It also shows how the emergent physics drives the gameplay.
prXuyMCgbTc.why: It is the go-to talk for anyone building falling-sand or pixel-physics simulations, and several commenters say they modeled their own engines on it.

pqzcCfUglws.summary: Audio of Charlie Munger's 1995 Harvard speech on the psychology of human misjudgment, laying out a framework of cognitive biases and mental models for decision making. It covers factors like incentives, social proof and denial.
pqzcCfUglws.why: HN regards it as a classic to revisit every few years for improving decisions and self-awareness.

p6K4iIMlouI.summary: Vim creator Bram Moolenaar's 2007 Google Tech Talk on habits for efficient text editing. He explains how to spot repetition and inefficiency, then use editor features to fix it.
p6K4iIMlouI.why: HN recommends it as a lasting philosophy for improving your editing process incrementally, and it was widely remembered after Moolenaar's death.

p7bzE1E5PMY.summary: An animated visualization of basic quantum mechanics using a free particle, with simulations based on the actual equations. It covers waves, particles, and how measurement collapses the wavefunction.
p7bzE1E5PMY.why: HN commenters call it one of the best visual explanations of the wave, particle and measurement relationship, free of silly metaphors.

p83QUZ1-P10.summary: The first video in Photon of Scoopex's Amiga hardware programming series. It shows how to set up an assembler and write a minimal 68000 program that waits for a left mouse click.
p83QUZ1-P10.why: Recommended as an approachable start to Amiga demo and 68000 assembly programming.

pLPpl2ISKTg.summary: A Last Week Tonight segment on pig butchering scams, in which long-con romance and investment fraud is run, often by trafficked workers. It explains how victims are groomed and interviews people who lost large sums.
pLPpl2ISKTg.why: Offered as an accessible, well-made explainer to share in threads on scam texts, crypto fraud and scam compounds.

pQ0CvjAJXz4.summary: Bryan Hunter's GigCityElixir 2023 talk on HCA Healthcare's Waterpark system, built on Elixir/Erlang. It describes how the architecture is distributed and fault-tolerant, with a multi-datacenter cluster and runtime code swapping.
pQ0CvjAJXz4.why: HN recommends it as a rare real-world look at a large fault-tolerant Erlang/Elixir system with no downtime in healthcare.

pXOK-ZVJMaU.summary: Patrick Stewart on the BBC's Parkinson talk show talks humorously about going bald, how it affected his career and relationships, and how he came to accept it.
pXOK-ZVJMaU.why: HN recommends it in hair-loss threads as a funny, inspiring example of accepting baldness.

plVk4NVIUh8.summary: A two-minute time-lapse from the Kishony Lab showing bacteria spreading across a giant petri dish with increasing antibiotic doses, evolving resistance as they go.
plVk4NVIUh8.why: HN links it as a visually striking demonstration of evolution and antibiotic resistance happening in days.

pOmXiapfCs8.summary: A 1985 interview by G. Edward Griffin with former KGB operative Yuri Bezmenov. He describes long-running Soviet efforts at ideological subversion and manipulation of US public opinion.
pOmXiapfCs8.why: HN commenters bring it up in threads on propaganda, influence operations and platforms like TikTok, saying it feels more relevant than ever.

pYXy-A4siMw.summary: Robert Miles gives a remastered introduction to AI safety, adapted from a talk in London. It lays out why advanced AI could go wrong and answers common objections.
pYXy-A4siMw.why: The default link for newcomers wanting an approachable, entertaining introduction to AI risk and alignment.

pkCLMl0e_0k.summary: David Beazley's PyCon 2019 tutorial derives the lambda calculus from the ground up in Python, using only single-argument functions. He builds booleans, numerals and more with no other language features.
pkCLMl0e_0k.why: HN calls it a brilliant, mind-bending introduction to lambda calculus for programmers.

ph8LyNIT9sg.summary: PS5 lead system architect Mark Cerny gives a deep dive into the PS5's architecture, covering its SSD, I/O, audio and design goals. He explains how removing bottlenecks shapes future games.
ph8LyNIT9sg.why: HN treats it as required viewing for understanding the PS5's SSD and architecture beyond raw specs.

p5_tpq5ejFQ.summary: The SIGGRAPH 2005 demo of dual photography from Stanford, which swaps the roles of projector and camera to render a scene from the light's point of view. It includes the reveal of a hidden playing card.
p5_tpq5ejFQ.why: Cited whenever threads discuss recovering hidden images or non-line-of-sight imaging, as a clear demonstration of light transport.

pN34FNbOKXc.summary: Eduardo Briceno gives a TEDx talk on mindset, contrasting fixed and growth views of ability. He argues that believing abilities can be developed encourages challenge, deliberate practice and grit.
pN34FNbOKXc.why: Recommended as a short, clear explanation of growth versus fixed mindset.

pqeJFYwnkjE.summary: Ward Cunningham explains the history and intent of the debt metaphor, which he coined while refactoring the WyCash product. He says debt means code reflecting an incomplete understanding of the problem, not sloppy programming.
pqeJFYwnkjE.why: HN links it as the authoritative correction to common misuse of the term technical debt, straight from its originator.

pagPuiuA9cY.summary: A beginner-focused tutorial on freehand knife sharpening with a single stone, aiming for a shaving-sharp edge in about five minutes.
pagPuiuA9cY.why: Recommended by commenters who say its practical, scientific explanations finally taught them how and why sharpening works.

p8u_k2LIZyo.summary: A walkthrough of the Quake III fast inverse square root, explaining where the constant 0x5f3759df comes from. It covers IEEE 754 floats, the bit hack that approximates a logarithm, and a Newton's method refinement.
p8u_k2LIZyo.why: HN recommends it as an approachable explanation that makes the famous algorithm finally make sense.

pHsuIaPbNbY.summary: Michael Betancourt's lecture at MLSS Iceland 2014 on efficient Bayesian inference with Hamiltonian Monte Carlo. It covers MCMC concepts and motivation and the problems of sampling in high-dimensional distributions.
pHsuIaPbNbY.why: HN people return to it as a clear primer on MCMC and HMC and on why high dimensions behave counterintuitively.

pMYYx_im5QI.summary: Novelist Daniel Suarez warns in a TED talk about autonomous robotic weapons and drones. He argues that taking the decision to kill out of human hands threatens democratic accountability and calls for a ban.
pMYYx_im5QI.why: Plugged repeatedly in AI and drone threads as a concise statement of the dangers of automated weapons.

pO4_Wlq8JeI.summary: Sasa Juric's EMPEX talk demonstrates Elixir and Erlang's process model and what makes the BEAM runtime distinctive, such as fault-tolerant parallelism by design.
pO4_Wlq8JeI.why: Recommended as the best short overview of why the BEAM and Elixir stand apart from other runtimes.

pX8BXH3SJn0.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on the NCAA, arguing that the organization profits enormously from college athletes while insisting they remain unpaid amateurs. It covers the money in college sports, including big-school athletic spending, and the case for paying athletes.
pX8BXH3SJn0.why: HN commenters cite it as a sharp, accessible primer on the NCAA's amateurism model and athlete compensation, including for readers outside the US.

pxBQLFLei70.summary: Admiral William McRaven's 2014 University of Texas commencement address, built around lessons from Navy SEAL training. It famously opens with the case for making your bed every morning.
pxBQLFLei70.why: Recommended in life-advice and motivation threads as worth watching in full, especially for its point about starting small by changing yourself.

p5Ac7ap_MAY.summary: Michael Oswald's documentary, based on Richard Werner's book, argues that Japan's 1990s crash was engineered by the central bank and powerful interests. It focuses on the Bank of Japan's hidden influence over the economy.
p5Ac7ap_MAY.why: HN commenters recommend it for a more cynical view of central bank power, though some caveat it as conspiracy-leaning.

pIgMTsQXg3Q.summary: Historia Civilis explains the constitution of ancient Athens, including its assembly, offices and use of sortition to choose leaders. It draws on Aristotle and Plutarch.
pIgMTsQXg3Q.why: Recommended in governance threads for showing how randomness and short terms prevented power concentration.

pL3Yzjk5R4M.summary: Nickolas Means tells the story of Lockheed's Skunk Works and how its engineers built the U-2, SR-71 and F-117 under tight deadlines and budgets. He draws lessons for modern software teams.
pL3Yzjk5R4M.why: HN recommends it as a well-done history of Skunk Works, popping up in SR-71 threads.

pUF5esTscZI.summary: CGP Grey explains the elegant ratio of A4 and the metric paper sizes, then zooms out across scales from the Planck length to the observable universe.
pUF5esTscZI.why: Loved for its zoom-out tour of physical scales and recommended alongside other paper-size and scale-of-the-universe discussions.

pdJQ8iVTwj8.summary: Lex Fridman's long podcast conversation with Chris Lattner, creator of Swift, LLVM and MLIR and co-founder of Modular. Topics include the Mojo language, the future of programming and AI, and hardware.
pdJQ8iVTwj8.why: HN points to it as the main place to hear Lattner's motivations and design ideas for Mojo, often in Mojo threads.

pdmODVYPDLA.summary: Kyle Hill of Because Science explains and demonstrates, using real cards, how Magic: The Gathering can be used to build a Turing machine, a computer inside the card game.
pdmODVYPDLA.why: HN links it as the accessible, hands-on demo behind the claim that Magic is Turing complete.

pnv5iKB2hl4.summary: Roman Mars gives a funny TED talk on vexillology, laying out five basic principles of good flag design and why many city flags fail them.
pnv5iKB2hl4.why: The canonical reference on flag and logo design principles, cited in branding and design threads.

pyX8kQ-JzHI.summary: The first lecture of Leonard Susskind's Stanford Continuing Studies course on modern physics, beginning with classical mechanics. It is the start of a six-quarter sequence on the theoretical foundations of physics.
pyX8kQ-JzHI.why: HN recommends Susskind as a very good explainer who uses real math at an accessible level, and links this lecture series for self-learners.

pKmSdY56VtY.summary: HERO is a short animated film made entirely in Blender to showcase the Grease Pencil 2D animation tools in Blender 2.8. It mixes hand-drawn 2D with a full 3D pipeline.
pKmSdY56VtY.why: HN points to it as an impressive demo of Blender's open-source 2D/3D hybrid animation and as a comparison for other 2D animation tools.

pSHj5UKSylk.summary: A two-hour extended interview in which Crash Bandicoot co-creator Andy Gavin tells how he and Jason Rubin built the game at Naughty Dog. It includes the custom Lisp tools used.
pSHj5UKSylk.why: HN recommends it as a fascinating hacker war story, especially in threads on Naughty Dog's custom Lisp languages GOOL and GOAL.

pSm7BcQHWXk.summary: A BBC Weird Nature clip about vervet monkeys in the Caribbean that drink alcohol, and how they split into heavy drinkers, social drinkers and teetotalers.
pSm7BcQHWXk.why: HN shares it as an amusing parallel to human drinking habits and as a possible window into addiction.

plcc6E-E1uU.summary: Lex Fridman interviews Harvard astrophysicist Avi Loeb about the interstellar object Oumuamua, aliens and black holes. Loeb lays out his argument that it may be an artifact rather than debris.
plcc6E-E1uU.why: HN recommends it as a good, non-sensational presentation of Loeb's actual argument, usually linked in Oumuamua threads.

pqQSwQLDIK8.summary: Nine minutes of unedited footage of a very busy bicycle and car crossing at Korte Prinsengracht and Haarlemmerstraat in Amsterdam. Cyclists, pedestrians and cars flow through without traffic lights.
pqQSwQLDIK8.why: Cited in urbanism and self-driving threads as a vivid example of dense mixed traffic working through infrastructure and culture.

p-I8GDklsN4.summary: A 1996 documentary on the twentieth-century American decline of public transport and the role of car companies and the highway lobby in it. It is best known for its account of GM's streetcar buyouts.
p-I8GDklsN4.why: HN cites it as the go-to documentary on how car-industry interests undermined US transit.

p3lsYlod5OU.summary: Lex Fridman talks with Tufts biologist Michael Levin about bioelectricity, embryogenesis, xenobots and how cells collectively pursue goals. They range into cognition, evolution and the possibility of aliens.
p3lsYlod5OU.why: HN links it as a long-form entry point to Levin's ideas on cancer, bioelectric signaling and intelligence beyond the brain, though one commenter finds some claims outlandish.

pEKq8jmckz0.summary: Robert Llewellyn of Fully Charged takes an early, 19-minute test drive of the Honda e electric car in Frankfurt. He looks at its acceleration, camera wing mirrors and tight turning circle.
pEKq8jmckz0.why: Shared in Honda e and camera-mirror threads as a look at the car's features and driving feel.

pNlq-EVld70.summary: Anders Hejlsberg introduces the native port of the TypeScript compiler, written in Go, which promises roughly 10x faster tooling. He demos compiling VS Code and explains where the speedup comes from.
pNlq-EVld70.why: Commenters cite it as the authoritative source for why the port is faster and why Go was chosen.

pPJf8KrvJXU.summary: Joel Spolsky, founder of Fog Creek Software and StackExchange, speaks at Y Combinator's Startup School in 2012. He shares his perspective on building startups.
pPJf8KrvJXU.why: HN recalls it as a well-liked talk from a respected founder, cited on startup ambition and on how few servers StackOverflow needed.

pT19VwBAqKA.summary: minutephysics, in collaboration with the US Census Bureau, explains differential privacy and why the 2020 census adds noise to protect individuals' data. It walks through how statistics can leak private information.
pT19VwBAqKA.why: Linked as the clearest technical explainer of differential privacy and the census, and of why aggregate data can still compromise privacy.

p_iZr2-Coqc.summary: A short documentary about the 1980 Lake Peigneur accident in Louisiana, where an oil rig drilled into a salt mine beneath the lake. The lake drained into the mine, creating a whirlpool that swallowed barges.
p_iZr2-Coqc.why: Linked in salt mine and industrial accident threads as a fascinating, quick account with striking footage.

pa5_tudyAF8.summary: A 41-minute factory tour showing how the BMW i3 electric car is built from start to finish, in the style of a Megafactories documentary. It shows a highly automated production line with carbon-fiber body construction and robots doing most of the work.
pa5_tudyAF8.why: Cited as a vivid example of modern, highly automated manufacturing with few workers, and of carmakers as robotics companies.

ph9O9yJoeZY.summary: Practical Engineering explains why San Francisco's Millennium Tower is sinking and tilting, covering how geology and foundation design (friction piles in the Colma Formation) affect skyscrapers. It also covers the fix being attempted.
ph9O9yJoeZY.why: HN commenters point to it as the well-made, detailed explanation of the Millennium Tower debacle whenever the tower comes up.

pq1XqP4-qOo.summary: Andrew Kelley's Zig SHOWTIME talk on an experiment to ship static Linux executables that can do graphics and gaming, followed by an interview. It covers the problems of Linux binary stability, dynamic linking and the graphics ABI.
pq1XqP4-qOo.why: HN cites it in threads on Linux desktop application distribution as a clear treatment of why binary compatibility and static linking are hard.

p3JLaF_4Tz8.summary: Andrew Huberman interviews Stanford addiction psychiatrist Dr. Anna Lembke about the biology and psychology of addiction to drugs, food, gambling, screens and more. They discuss dopamine, the opioid crisis, and her book Dopamine Nation.
p3JLaF_4Tz8.why: HN people send it to others in addiction and digital-habits threads as an expert explanation of dopamine baselines.

pP44EPBMb8A.summary: A Kurzgesagt animated explainer on how humanity could build a Dyson sphere, a swarm of structures capturing the sun's energy. It covers using Mercury's materials and a step-by-step construction approach.
pP44EPBMb8A.why: HN links it as a nice intro to what a realistic Dyson swarm would require, and as a companion to megastructure discussions.

pTbSMKGQ_rU.summary: A two-hour complete longplay of the 1993 MS-DOS puzzle game The Incredible Machine, in which players assemble Rube Goldberg contraptions to complete simple tasks.
pTbSMKGQ_rU.why: Used as a nostalgic link to a beloved childhood game, and as an example of a tight failure-iteration learning loop.

pm5xxlajTW0.summary: The full, long-form FRONTLINE interview with Steve Bannon, recorded in 2019 for the documentary series on the Obama-to-Trump era. He discusses his populist politics, the Trump campaign and White House, and his view of the establishment.
pm5xxlajTW0.why: HN people recommend it as an unfiltered way to understand Bannon's worldview and the populist movement, and praise PBS for releasing full interviews.

pmfHHLfbjNQ.summary: James Houston's entry to Radiohead's Nude remix contest, performing the 6/8, 63bpm song on obsolete hardware such as hard drives, a dot matrix printer, a scanner and a ZX Spectrum.
pmfHHLfbjNQ.why: It is the canonical example HN brings up in threads about music hacks on floppy drives, printers and other junk hardware.

pyMNIFZTQkg.summary: A 3-minute CGI animated sci-fi short by Dima Fedotov. An automated war system keeps a lone bomber attacking a long-dead city after humanity has been wiped out, until life finds a way to survive.
pyMNIFZTQkg.why: Cited as a vivid illustration of autonomous weapons and machines that keep running after their creators are gone.

p45T7U5oi9Q.summary: A 1940 Bell Telephone educational short teaching customers how to use their new dial phones and why the change was happening. It is a period piece about rolling out a new technology to ordinary people.
p45T7U5oi9Q.why: Cited as a charming example of the effort once made to teach the public a new technology, in threads about phones and teaching seniors.

pBTvmrRGlbE.summary: Geoff Marshall explains a running gag about London Underground stair signs claiming that the climb equals 15 floors, regardless of how many steps there actually are.
pBTvmrRGlbE.why: Cited as the explanation for the oddly inaccurate tube staircase signs, and as an example of Marshall's station-detail videos.

pBiWtJJN5zk.summary: Jason Perkins's talk at Vintage Computer Festival East 2020 compares the user interface of the Xerox Star with that of the Apple Lisa. It covers editing documents, the Star's mouse and a Q&A.
pBiWtJJN5zk.why: Shared as a recent, detailed comparison of the two early GUIs and where their conventions differ.

pKcmNGvaDUs.summary: A 2016 documentary by Igor Lopatonok that gives a historical perspective on Ukraine's divisions, the 2004 Orange Revolution and the 2014 Maidan uprising. It argues that Western media painted Russia as the sole perpetrator.
pKcmNGvaDUs.why: In 2022 some HN commenters shared it for historical context on Ukraine, usually with caveats about its bias and accuracy.

pRjsu9-Vznc.summary: GoldenSound publishes music on Tidal to test MQA, a deep dive into the format's claims and problems including its leaky filter. Testing begins around the 5:45 mark.
pRjsu9-Vznc.why: Cited in audio-streaming threads as a critical breakdown showing MQA is neither lossless nor transparent.

pRlh8LX4kQI.summary: A Google I/O 2019 talk explaining the architecture of Linux on Chromebooks (Crostini), a sandboxed Linux development environment built on containers inside a VM, with demos and design rationale.
pRlh8LX4kQI.why: Referenced in security discussions as an example of defense-in-depth sandboxing for a desktop Linux environment.

pVI_smLgTY0.summary: PewDiePie describes switching to Linux and encourages viewers to do the same. It is a casual, enthusiastic video aimed at a mainstream audience.
pVI_smLgTY0.why: HN mentions it as a sign of Linux reaching millions of non-technical viewers, with some finding it funny and others fascinating.

pWI5aVKvkCg.summary: Ryuichi Sakamoto's piece Blu, performed by the Tokyo Philharmonic Orchestra. It was written to commemorate the 50th anniversary of the Aoyama clothing company.
pWI5aVKvkCg.why: Offered as calm piano-led music for programming and shared as a personal favorite and memorial to Sakamoto.

pcVGqtmd2wM.summary: Tom Scott visits Peachtree City, Georgia, which has about a hundred miles of dedicated golf cart paths that serve as an alternative to driving. He explains how the network works as a quasi-transit system that keeps cars off the roads.
pcVGqtmd2wM.why: HN uses it as the go-to example of low-speed vehicle infrastructure in a US suburb, in threads on e-bikes, EVs and autonomous cars.

pgaEE27nsQw.summary: A 2013 research demo of simulated bipedal creatures whose natural gaits are found by optimizing muscle-based controllers, with no motion capture or keyframe animation. It shows physics-based walking and running emerging from musculoskeletal models.
pgaEE27nsQw.why: HN cites it as an earlier, smoother precedent whenever new learned-locomotion or simulated-walking work appears.

pnmRYRRDbuw.summary: NonCompete's video examines the alt-right pipeline and a 'pyramid of violence' running from implicit bias through edgy racist humor to real violence. It uses the PewDiePie controversy and Charlottesville as case studies.
pnmRYRRDbuw.why: Pointed to in radicalization threads as a good explanation of how online humor can funnel people toward extremism.

psAXMqxwol8.summary: Retired submarine captain David Marquet explains, with drawings, how he turned the USS Santa Fe around by treating his crew as leaders rather than followers. It summarizes the ideas of his book Turn the Ship Around.
psAXMqxwol8.why: Recommended as a short, illustrated take on empowering teams instead of giving orders.

ptjedOZEXPM.summary: Dan Bornstein's Google I/O 2008 talk on the internals of Dalvik, the virtual machine that runs Android code. It covers the motivation for its design, the dex format and its register-based interpreter, plus tips for writing code that suits the platform.
ptjedOZEXPM.why: HN points to it as the primary source on Dalvik's dex bytecode, register-based design and memory-saving choices.

p1nwLilQy64.summary: A two-minute clip of Steve Jobs at WWDC 2007 introducing the plan for iPhone third-party apps as web apps built on Safari and Ajax. It shows the original vision before the native SDK and App Store.
p1nwLilQy64.why: HN cites it in platform-power and PWA debates as proof that Apple originally wanted the future of apps to be on the web.

pBdGOrcUEg8.summary: A very short clip titled Criminal Conspiracy Notes, apparently the scene from The Wire in which Stringer Bell scolds his associates for taking written notes at a meeting.
pBdGOrcUEg8.why: HN uses it as a joke or warning shorthand, the 'Stringer Bell warning', about leaving written evidence of illegal plans.

pJdrlWR-yFM.summary: Top Gear segment in which Hammond and May try to turn a Reliant Robin into a space shuttle. Launching is easy, but landing it safely is the problem.
pJdrlWR-yFM.why: Mostly referenced as a funny aside when space shuttle or small cars come up.

pM70TROZQsI.summary: Shrek Retold is a crowdsourced, scene-for-scene remake of Shrek made by over 200 creators, each redoing a short section in their own style.
pM70TROZQsI.why: Mentioned as an example of a crowd-made reproduction of a film whose quality varies wildly.

pQHX-SjgQvQ.summary: A classic Norwegian TV comedy sketch from NRK's show Oystein og jeg, subtitled in English, in which a monk calls a helpdesk to learn how to use a book instead of a scroll.
pQHX-SjgQvQ.why: HN drops it as a joke whenever threads touch on new interfaces, books or technology confusing users.

pQQTScuApWk.summary: A 1993 VHS demo of Lucid Energize, a database-backed, incremental C/C++ programming environment built on XEmacs. It shows features like incremental compilation, live debugging and hyperlinked output.
pQQTScuApWk.why: HN cites it constantly as evidence that modern IDE and LSP-style features existed in the early 90s.

pRSWdtoUAjo.summary: A one-minute demonstration of iOS 14's new paste notification, which revealed popular apps silently reading the clipboard each time they were opened. It credits the mysk research write-up.
pRSWdtoUAjo.why: HN cites it as evidence that many mainstream apps, not just TikTok, were snooping on clipboard contents.

pU9sHwNKc2c.summary: Tom Scott explains why subtitles often differ from dubbed dialogue, covering how translation, timing and reading speed shape each. It features translators and voice talent working in several languages.
pU9sHwNKc2c.why: Cited in subtitle threads for its explanation of why subtitles are condensed and adapted rather than literal.

pWdd6_ZxX8c.summary: A very short clip of the famous 'that's just, like, your opinion, man' line from The Big Lebowski.
pWdd6_ZxX8c.why: Used as a joke reply to dismissive or opinionated comments.

pWgyy_rlmag.summary: A scene from Moneyball in which Brad Pitt's character argues with scouts who pick players on intangible impressions instead of performance data. It is a four-minute clip.
pWgyy_rlmag.why: Invoked as shorthand for hiring and investing by gut feel and appearances instead of what actually predicts results.

pZwvrxVavnQ.summary: A short animation from Thames Valley Police that explains sexual consent by comparing it to offering someone a cup of tea.
pZwvrxVavnQ.why: Mostly invoked as an analogy or joke, including in discussions of opt-in consent and voluntary transactions.

pb5_F4_Eod8.summary: A Rheinmetall promo clip of its truck-mounted Skynex air defence system engaging a swarm of eight small drones with a 35mm revolver gun.
pb5_F4_Eod8.why: Used as an example of existing anti-drone-swarm defences in threads on drone warfare.

pdR7WW3XR9c.summary: A short clip of Margaret Thatcher in Parliament in 1990 arguing that economic reforms benefited everyone even as the rich-poor gap widened. She says her opponents would rather the poor be poorer if it meant the rich were less rich.
pdR7WW3XR9c.why: Commenters link it as a shorthand for an argument about inequality, absolute versus relative prosperity, quoting her line in threads about taxes and wealth.

pdz5kCaCRFM.summary: The official music video for Blues Traveler's song Hook, remastered in HD. The song is known for using the melody of Pachelbel's Canon while its lyrics comment on how hooks work.
pdz5kCaCRFM.why: HN mentions it mainly as a music example in threads on shared melodies and on how to craft a compelling hook, with a few jokes.

pjvQFtlNQ-M.summary: A very short clip from the film Anchorman in which Ron Burgundy declares that Sex Panther works 60 percent of the time, every time.
pjvQFtlNQ-M.why: Used purely as a joke reply, typically when someone cites an unreliable or only-sometimes-true claim.

pnbJEg9r1o8.summary: Physics Girl shows a vortex phenomenon (a falaco soliton) that can be reproduced in a pool on a sunny day. Two vortices are created with plates and made visible with food coloring.
pnbJEg9r1o8.why: Cited as a concrete demonstration of vortex linkage, and as a better source link than the original submission.

pnsizkVjGm8.summary: A roughly one-minute TV clip in which a guest accidentally breaks a rare, one-of-a-kind wax cylinder recording on camera.
pnsizkVjGm8.why: Shared as a darkly funny moment of televised schadenfreude in threads about early audio formats and cylinder archives.

poyf3Cnb-MQ.summary: A nearly five-hour live stream from Martin Shkreli with no description. HN mentions use it to show him working in Excel.
poyf3Cnb-MQ.why: Mostly cited as a reference for watching Shkreli use spreadsheets, not as a recommendation.

psL_5RIBqnY.summary: Apple's full WWDC 2019 keynote, announcing iOS 13 with Dark Mode, watchOS 6, iPadOS, macOS Catalina, the new Mac Pro and the Pro Display XDR.

pzXlUw2WhcE.summary: SpaceX footage of the Grasshopper vertical takeoff and landing test vehicle making its first roughly 6-foot hop in McGregor, Texas, on September 21, 2012. It was an early step toward a reusable Falcon 9 first stage.
